messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty - HIGH - AuroraFin (dedicated tenant) latency/error spike detected. 90th p99 RPS > SLO threshold, error rate rising. link: https://redwood.internal/alerts/2102345678
PagerDuty: Alert triggered and routed to eng-oncall. Escalation policy: oncall -> sre -> lead.
maya: ack, I'm taking first look. pulling tail logs now. can someone confirm customer name: AuroraFin?
liam: +1 AuroraFin. Their reserved pool shows increased scheduling delays and KV cache misses. looks like burst queue is backing up.
sre_jamie: oncall joining. maya hands off if you already have logs.
maya: handing off to @sre_jamie. paste logs snippet below.
maya: ```
2026-03-14T15:10:02Z ERROR tenant=aurorafin handler=serve request_id=abc123 latency_ms=2450 err=timeout
2026-03-14T15:10:03Z WARN tenant=aurorafin kvcache_miss=0.78 batch_size=1 pool_util=0.92
2026-03-14T15:10:05Z INFO tenant=aurorafin enqueue_delay_ms=1200 reserved_pool_queue_len=42
```
liam: Looks like reserved_pool_queue_len jumped after a sudden traffic burst from a partner workflow. Also seeing some model variant fallbacks which increase latency.
oncall_nikhil: is dedicated autoscaler triggered? I see no new nodes coming up.
sre_jamie: autoscaler didn't scale because pool was at max_reserved for that tenant. showing quota cap at 8 GPUs.
liam: propose temporary mitigation: 1) enable tenant burst-bypass to spill requests to shared-hosted cluster for non-sensitive routes; 2) enable KV-cache forced warm for AuroraFin; 3) increase reserved cap to 10 GPUs (manual override) while we investigate.
sre_jamie: Agree. Can do 2 & 3. 1 requires product signoff for data-path routing - cc @support_emma to notify customer if we reroute.
sre_jamie: running manual override now: `infractl reserved set-capacity --tenant aurorafin --count 10 --reason "auto-mitigate latency spike"`
deploy-bot: Command accepted. Starting capacity provisioning. job_id=prov-5589. ETA ~3m.
liam: enabling KV-cache warm policy for tenant. `configctl set tenant.aurorafin.kvcache.warm=true --ttl 600`
config-bot: KV-cache warm enabled for aurorafin.
sre_jamie: watching metrics. queue length dropping from 42 -> 18. p95 latency down from 2.4s -> 0.9s in last 90s.
support_emma: support@example.com is on standby to message AuroraFin. Recommend we tell them we saw a transient capacity cap and we scaled up; offering post-incident summary.
maya: any idea what caused the spike? liam mentioned partner workflow?
liam: preliminary: a partner batch job (cron) misconfigured and spiked concurrent requests x6 for a 2m window. We'll dig through ingress logs.
PagerDuty: Alert acknowledged by maya, escalated to sre_jamie at 2102345705.
incident-bot: NOTE: page auto-escalated to lead after 5m of no manual resolution. escalation executed.
liam: mitigation holding. monitoring for 10 more minutes before we close. will run extra telemetry sweep for model fallbacks.
sre_jamie: provisioning complete, reserved capacity increased to 10 GPUs, no longer hitting quota. queue trimmed to <5, error rate back to baseline.
support_emma: emailed AuroraFin with a short heads-up and ETA for a postmortem.
oncall_nikhil: handoff in 15m to next oncall (sre_jamie -> oncall_nikhil) for follow-up?
sre_jamie: I'll stay until metrics stable then handoff. summary: root cause suspected partner load spike + reserved capacity cap; mitigation: manual capacity bump + KV-cache warm + per-tenant routing avoided. Next: persist cap change while we evaluate traffic pattern, add ingress rate-limit to prevent future cron spikes.
PagerDuty: Incident resolved.
incident-bot: Incident resolved and page closed at 2102345966. :white_check_mark: 
support_emma: leaving a note in #customer-success and creating a support ticket for AuroraFin follow-up.
